paraphrase: The hagiography tells of feats: he ate a thousand plantains that a king offered to test him (10.51); his toenail shone to light his work (16.6); he set in place, for a bathing ghāṭ, a huge rock that many men had brought with difficulty (16.7).
speaker: Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya
notes: Summary of separate verses; the rock episode's details paraphrased loosely. checked against the Devanāgarī e-text in sources_raw/raw_etexts/vedAntam/dvaitam (github.com/sanskrit/raw_etexts); numbering follows that copy and may differ in other editions

paraphrase: The chiefs of the gods praised him — 'homage to you, lord of breath; homage, Hanumān, dearest to Rāma; homage, Bhīma, dear to Kṛṣṇa; homage, Madhva; grant us right vision' — and rained fragrant flowers on Ānandatīrtha, the dearest of Hari's beloved.
speaker: Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya

paraphrase: (At his renunciation) he became an ascetic entitled to the japa of the praṇava, whose three measures the wise say end in the endless; and he was given the name Pūrṇabodha, befitting the height of his qualities.
speaker: Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya

paraphrase: Resolved upon by his teacher for the rule of the kingdom of Vedānta learning, he was consecrated with waters; and the name 'Ānandatīrtha' spoken by the teacher became fitting for him who was a vessel of the supreme Bliss and made the blissful śāstra.
speaker: Nārāyaṇa Paṇḍitācārya
